Requirement: The system shall implement three independent logical ECUs.
PassCriterion: All three execute their own state and message-processing logic.

Requirement: Each ECU shall have a defined responsibility and interface.
PassCriterion: Interface documentation exists for every ECU.

Requirement: ECU application logic shall be independent of the physical CAN driver.
PassCriterion: The same core logic runs against a virtual and hardware transport adapter.

Requirement: Each ECU shall initialize into a defined safe state.
PassCriterion: Startup tests verify outputs and communication state before normal operation.

Requirement: Each ECU shall support reset and reinitialization.
PassCriterion: After reset, the ECU returns to a defined state and resumes permitted communication.

Requirement: Runtime behavior shall be observable through logs and diagnostics.
PassCriterion: Every injected fault produces a traceable event or documented reason for no event.

Requirement: Every application message shall have a defined CAN identifier and payload layout.
PassCriterion: No duplicate IDs among messages that coexist in the same network configuration.

Requirement: Every signal shall define its bit position, width, byte order, scaling, offset and valid range where applicable.
PassCriterion: Encoding and decoding tests match published test vectors.

Requirement: Periodic messages shall use configured transmission intervals.
PassCriterion: Measured intervals remain within defined tolerances under the specified test load.

Requirement: Receivers shall validate message identifiers, payload lengths and signal ranges.
PassCriterion: Malformed or invalid inputs are rejected or handled according to documented rules.

Requirement: Receivers shall detect stale data and missing periodic messages.
PassCriterion: Timeout tests detect missing messages within the configured deadline.

Requirement: The implementation shall handle transmit queue saturation and receive buffer exhaustion.
PassCriterion: Overflow is detected, counted and handled without memory corruption.

Requirement: The network shall define message priorities and an arbitration-aware ID allocation scheme.
PassCriterion: Design documentation explains priority choices and worst-case considerations.

Requirement: The application shall expose counters for transmission errors, receive errors, timeouts and dropped frames where measurable.
PassCriterion: Counters are observable and tested.

Requirement: The hardware implementation shall handle controller error states and bus-off recovery.
PassCriterion: Hardware tests demonstrate fault detection and documented recovery behavior.

Requirement: The protocol shall support versioned message definitions or an explicit compatibility policy.
PassCriterion: Incompatible message versions are detected or rejected according to the policy.

Requirement: The Powertrain ECU shall publish simulated engine RPM and vehicle speed.
PassCriterion: Values update at configured rates and remain within documented limits.

Requirement: The Body ECU shall manage door and lighting states.
PassCriterion: Input events produce the expected state changes and CAN messages.

Requirement: The Dashboard ECU shall consume vehicle signals and generate display and warning states.
PassCriterion: Displayed values agree with valid source signals; stale data produces a defined warning.

Requirement: Each ECU shall implement an explicit state machine.
PassCriterion: Valid and invalid state transitions are covered by tests.

Requirement: The Dashboard ECU shall distinguish normal, stale and invalid signals.
PassCriterion: Each condition maps to a documented behavior.

Requirement: ECUs shall start and stop independently without crashing other logical ECUs.
PassCriterion: Resetting or stopping one ECU does not corrupt other ECU state.

Requirement: Signals shall have defined startup values and invalid/unavailable representations where needed.
PassCriterion: Startup and invalid-value test cases produce predictable results.

Requirement: The system shall support configurable simulation scenarios.
PassCriterion: A scenario file can control inputs and timing without changing application source code.

Requirement: Each ECU shall maintain a diagnostic trouble code (DTC) store.
PassCriterion: Defined faults create the expected diagnostic records.

Requirement: Faults shall have defined detection, confirmation and clearing rules.
PassCriterion: Tests verify transitions from normal to faulted and back.

Requirement: A diagnostic client shall be able to request supported diagnostic information.
PassCriterion: Valid requests return correct data; invalid requests return defined errors.

Requirement: The system shall record relevant fault occurrence and recovery events.
PassCriterion: Logs identify the ECU, fault type and event sequence.

Requirement: Diagnostic requests shall have timeouts and malformed-request handling.
PassCriterion: Invalid or incomplete requests do not crash an ECU.

Requirement: The diagnostic system shall expose supported services and data identifiers.
PassCriterion: A protocol document lists services, request formats and responses.

Requirement: The project shall implement a subset of UDS-inspired diagnostic services.
PassCriterion: At minimum, read supported data and read or clear DTCs through a documented interface.

Requirement: Diagnostic access control shall be documented if protected services are implemented.
PassCriterion: Protected operations reject unauthorized requests in the selected threat model.

Requirement: The test environment shall be able to stop or suppress selected periodic messages.
PassCriterion: The receiving ECU detects the resulting timeout.

Requirement: The system shall support out-of-range and stale signal injection.
PassCriterion: The receiving application follows its documented rejection or fallback rules.

Requirement: The system shall support independent ECU restart simulation.
PassCriterion: Restart behavior and message recovery are observable.

Requirement: The system shall support invalid diagnostic requests.
PassCriterion: Invalid requests receive a defined response or controlled rejection.

Requirement: The system shall simulate a CAN bus outage.
PassCriterion: Communication loss is detected, and recovery behavior is tested.

Requirement: The system shall detect queue overflows and resource exhaustion.
PassCriterion: Failures are counted and handled without undefined behavior.

Requirement: The system shall generate repeatable fault scenarios.
PassCriterion: The same scenario produces comparable event sequences across repeated runs.

Requirement: The physical implementation shall test controller error states and bus-off recovery.
PassCriterion: A documented hardware test validates the actual controller behavior.

Requirement: Periodic message scheduling
PassCriterion: Support configurable 10 ms, 20 ms, 100 ms and 1 s message periods.

Requirement: Receive processing latency
PassCriterion: Measure latency from frame reception to application handling; establish and document a target per deployment.

Requirement: Timeout detection
PassCriterion: Detect a missing message within its configured timeout plus a documented scheduling tolerance.

Requirement: CPU utilization
PassCriterion: Measure worst observed load under nominal and fault-injection scenarios.

Requirement: Buffer management
PassCriterion: Demonstrate bounded memory usage during sustained operation.

Requirement: Long-duration stability
PassCriterion: Run a continuous simulation for at least 2 hours without crashes, deadlocks or unexplained resource growth.
